entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.1-2Chr.9.12">2Ch 9:1-12</reference> <hi type="italic">The visit of the queen of Sheba</hi>. Cf. 1Ki 10:1-13. - This event is narrated as a practical proof of Solomon’s extraordinary wisdom. The narrative agrees so exactly in both texts, with the exception of some few quite unimportant differences, that we must regard them as literal extracts from an original document which they have used in common. For the commentary on this section, see on 1Ki 10:1-13.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.13-2Chr.9.21">2Ch 9:13-21</reference> <div eID="gen5966" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5967" type="x-p"/> Solomon’s revenue in gold, and the use he made of it. Cf. 1Ki 10:14-22, and the commentary there on this section, which is identical in both narratives, with the exception of some trifling differences. Before מביאים והסּחרים the relative pronoun is to be supplied: “and what the merchants brought.” As to the derivation of the word פּחות, which comes from the Aramaic form פּחה, governor (<reference osisRef="2Chr.9.14">2Ch 9:14</reference>), see on Hag 1:1. - תּרשׁישׁ הלכות אניּות, in <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.21">2Ch 9:21</reference>, ships going to Tarshish, is an erroneous paraphrase of תּרשׁישׁ אניּות, Tarshish-ships, i.e., ships built for long sea voyages; for the fleet did not go to Tartessus in Spain, but to Ophir in Southern Arabia (see on 1Ki 9:26.). All the rest has been explained in the commentary on 1 Kings 10.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.22-2Chr.9.24">2Ch 9:22-24</reference> <div eID="gen5967" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5968" type="x-p"/> In <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.22-2Chr.9.28">2Ch 9:22-28</reference>, all that remained to be said of Solomon’s royal glory, his riches, his wisdom, and his revenues, is in conclusion briefly summed up, as in 1Ki 10:23-29. From <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.25">2Ch 9:25</reference> onwards, the account given in the Chronicle diverges from that in 1Ki 10:26., in so far that what is narrated in 1Ki 10:26-28 concerning Solomon’s chariots and horses, and his trade with Egypt in horses, is here partly replaced by statements similar in import to those in 1 Kings 5, because the former matters had been already treated of in Chr. <reference osisRef="2Chr.1.14">2Ch 1:14</reference>-17.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.25-2Chr.9.28">2Ch 9:25-28</reference> <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.25">2Ch 9:25</reference> does not correspond to the passage 1Ki 10:26, but in contents and language agrees with 1Ki 5:6, and <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.26">2Ch 9:26</reference> with 1Ki 5:1. Only the general estimate of Solomon’s riches in gold and silver, in <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.27">2Ch 9:27</reference>, repeated from <reference osisRef="2Chr.1.15">2Ch 1:15</reference>, corresponds to 1Ki 10:27. Finally, in <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.28">2Ch 9:28</reference> the whole description is rounded off; all that has already been said in <reference osisRef="2Chr.1.16">2Ch 1:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Chr.1.17">2Ch 1:17</reference> as to the trade in horses with Egypt (1Ki 10:28-29) being drawn together into one general statement.
entries.content_plain: 2Ch 9:25-28 2Ch 9:25 does not correspond to the passage 1Ki 10:26, but in contents and language agrees with 1Ki 5:6, and 2Ch 9:26 with 1Ki 5:1. Finally, in 2Ch 9:28 the whole description is rounded off; all that has already been said in 2Ch 1:16 , 2Ch 1:17 as to the trade in horses with Egypt (1Ki 10:28-29) being drawn together into one general statement.
